h: Rivers, Railways and a Forest Discovery Centre
p: Wyre Forest is a wonderful place to explore at your own pace, and the Wyre Forest Discovery Centre at Callow Hill is a handy base, with trails, play areas and information about the forest's wildlife. Keep an eye out for deer and, in the right season, the woods are alive with birdsong.

Bewdley is a gem of a riverside town, with Georgian buildings along the Severn and a handsome bridge by Thomas Telford. The Bewdley Museum tells the story of the town's crafts and trades, and it's a nice, quiet stop after a busy morning in the trees.

The Severn Valley Railway connects Bewdley with Kidderminster and Bridgnorth, passing through gorgeous countryside along the way. Upper Arley, a pretty village on the line, is a lovely place to hop off and stroll along the river. A little south, Stourport-on-Severn has its Georgian canal basins and a lively riverside.
Harvington Hall, a moated Elizabethan manor near Kidderminster, is famous for its priest holes, the hidden hiding places used to conceal Catholic priests, and makes for a fascinating visit.
For the treetops, set aside a couple of hours and give yourselves time to park and get to the briefing. Wear grippy shoes and comfortable clothes, and bring water and a light jacket.
First-timers should take the early sections slowly and listen to the instructors. With practice, the clip-on routine becomes second nature, and you'll be flying through the trees in no time.
